newsitem.title: UK: Japanese stocks in London pick up on yen's slide.
newsitem.headline: Japanese stocks in London pick up on yen's slide.

text.p: Japanese stocks in London moved ahead on Tuesday after lower than expected U.S. wage inflation data sent the yen lower against the dollar, traders said.
The Nikkei 50 index was up 27.19 or 2.07 percent at 1,340.42 by 1612 GMT, while March Nikkei 225 futures on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange were 700 points higher at 17,950.0.
Blue-chip exporters were the main beneficiaries as the yen fell to 121.30 against the dollar from Monday's close of 119.50.
"This afternoon we've seen quite aggresive buying of some of the blue chips," one trader said.
He cited Sharp as the principal gainer. Others were NEC and Toyota.
"I'd expect a much firmer opening in Tokyo," another trader said. The Nikkei 225 average closed up 461.67 points at 17,796.57.

Interest was also shown in the banks after their recent fall on the back of worries over their financial health. Traders said buying interest was restricted to stocks benefiting directly from the yen's fall. "As far as the broader market is concerned, there's not a great deal of interest. If it's not dollar related, it's not moving."
The U.S. employment cost index (ECI) was up 0.8 percent for the fourth quarter of 1996 versus expectations of 0.9 percent.
